Fixes the white GUI on a fresh install, and makes the READY banner honest.

### Fixed
- **White GUI after a clean install.** JDownloader shows a "you have changed the look and feel to FlatLaf Dark — restart to apply" dialog on some fresh installs. The container's dialog agent didn't recognise that dialog, so it sat there unanswered: JD kept running with the default light look-and-feel (a white GUI) even though the dark theme was fully installed. The agent now confirms that dialog — matched on its text (locale-tolerant), answered with the restart-affirming button — and JD restarts itself once into the full dark theme. If the dialog ever appears with button labels the agent doesn't know, it now asks the container for one polite JD restart instead of leaving the GUI stuck, and logs the dialog's exact title and text so it can be matched precisely in the next release. (Deliberate side effect: manually changing the look-and-feel in the GUI now also triggers the restart that applies it.)
- **The READY banner could lie.** It used to fire once JD's API port was up and the patched FlatLaf jar existed on disk — which says nothing about whether the theme was actually *applied* (in the bug above, the banner fired while the GUI was white). The agent now records the actually-active look-and-feel, and `JDOWNLOADER IS READY` only prints when the expected theme is genuinely applied. If that can't be verified within ~10 minutes, the log now says so honestly (`JDOWNLOADER IS UP (theme NOT verified)`) with a pointer to the relevant log lines, instead of printing the same READY banner.
- **Unknown forced dialogs are now logged.** Any JD dialog the agent doesn't recognise is logged once with its verbatim title and text — so if JDownloader ever introduces another forced dialog, the container log carries exactly the strings needed to fix it, instead of a guess from a screenshot.

### Hardened
- **Bootstrap download.** The first-start download of `JDownloader.jar` is now retried (3×) and validated as a real jar (a captive portal or DNS hijack serving an HTML page no longer ends up saved as the launcher). If all attempts fail, the log shows a loud, repeating error banner instead of exiting silently to an empty desktop.
- Dialog auto-confirm now has per-window click guards (no rapid re-clicking), and the agent's state markers are wiped on every container boot *and* before every JD launch, so a crash-looping JD can't inherit stale "theme applied" state.

### Update
Pull `ghcr.io/junkerderprovinz/jdownloader:latest` (or `junkerderprovinz/jdownloader:latest` on Docker Hub) and recreate the container — in Unraid: **Force Update**. On a fresh install, wait for the `JDOWNLOADER IS READY` banner in the container log; it now genuinely means the dark theme is on screen.
